stem: Which is the most sensitive way to assess a child with acute abdominal pain?

options.text: Repeated clinical examination by the same doctor

explanation: Repeated clinical examination by the same doctor is the most sensitive way to assess a child with acute abdominal pain. Serial assessments let the clinician detect subtle but important changes over time, which often provides more diagnostic value than a single test.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because a single CT scan may help in selected cases, but it is not the most sensitive overall approach for assessing acute abdominal pain in children.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because liver function tests can support the assessment, but they do not offer the highest sensitivity for identifying the cause of acute abdominal pain.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because repeated examinations by the same doctor allow serial comparison and detection of subtle changes, making this the most sensitive assessment tool.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a plain abdominal X-ray has limited sensitivity and only a narrow role in most children with acute abdominal pain.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a one-off ultrasound can be useful, but a single imaging test is less sensitive than repeated clinical examination over time.

source.hint: Think about the value of continuity in physical assessment over time.
